items.stem: Where does the energy in almost every ecosystem originally come from?
items.explanation: Energy enters almost every ecosystem as sunlight. The Sun is the original source of energy for nearly all living things.

items.stem: An organism that makes its own food, usually using sunlight, is called what?
items.explanation: A producer, also called an autotroph, makes its own food, usually through photosynthesis.

items.stem: Which type of organism cannot make its own food and must eat other organisms?
items.explanation: A consumer, also called a heterotroph, cannot make food and gets energy by eating other organisms.

items.stem: A rabbit eats only plants. What kind of consumer is it?
items.explanation: A herbivore eats only plants. A rabbit that eats grass and leaves is a herbivore.

items.stem: What do decomposers do in an ecosystem?

options.text: They hunt and kill live prey
They break down dead matter and return materials to the environment
They add brand new energy to the ecosystem

items.explanation: Decomposers break down waste and dead organisms, returning raw materials to the environment for producers to reuse.

items.stem: What does a food chain show?

options.text: Every organism that lives in a region
One path of energy flow through an ecosystem
Only the decomposers in an ecosystem
The weather patterns of an ecosystem

items.explanation: A food chain shows one single path of energy as it flows from one organism to the next.

items.stem: How is a food web different from a food chain?

options.text: It has no producers in it
It shows only one path of energy
It leaves out all the consumers
It shows many overlapping food chains at once

items.explanation: A food web combines many overlapping food chains to show all the paths energy can take through an ecosystem.

items.stem: About how much of the energy at one feeding level is passed on to the next level up?
items.explanation: Only about 10% of the energy at a level moves to the next level. The rest is used for life processes or lost as heat.

items.stem: At which level of an energy pyramid is the most energy available?
items.explanation: The greatest amount of energy is at the producer level, at the base of the pyramid. Energy shrinks toward the top.

items.stem: Why are there usually far fewer top predators than plants in an ecosystem?

options.text: Top predators are simply larger animals
Much less energy is available at the higher feeding levels
Plants only grow during certain seasons
Top predators do not need to eat very often

items.explanation: Because only about 10% of energy passes up each level, there is far less energy at the top, so it supports fewer organisms.
